boundary_definitions.description: Traffic crossing a host network interface is filtered before reaching local services.
boundary_definitions.name: Host firewall

boundary_definitions.description: File-service sessions resist downgrade, relay, and unsigned exchange.
boundary_definitions.name: SMB session security

boundary_definitions.description: Directory authentication and queries receive integrity and transport protection.
boundary_definitions.name: LDAP channel security

boundary_definitions.description: Legacy authentication negotiation and resulting sessions reject weak protection.
boundary_definitions.name: NTLM session security

boundary_definitions.description: Remote-management traffic and credentials are protected across the management channel.
boundary_definitions.name: WinRM secure management

boundary_definitions.description: Interactive remote administration enforces pre-authentication, protected transport, and restricted rights.
boundary_definitions.name: RDP secure access

boundary_definitions.description: Host protection continuously prevents and blocks malicious behavior.
boundary_definitions.name: Malware protection stack

boundary_definitions.description: Administrative credentials and elevation transitions are isolated and mediated.
known_exclusions: account renaming and cosmetic identity changes
boundary_definitions.name: Privileged credential and execution boundary

boundary_definitions.description: Execution policy admits only trusted applications.
boundary_definitions.name: Application control

boundary_definitions.description: Interpreted and active content is constrained by enforceable policy.
boundary_definitions.name: Script control

boundary_definitions.description: Network exchanges require approved confidentiality and integrity protection.
boundary_definitions.name: Transport cryptography

boundary_definitions.description: Stored data is cryptographically protected from offline or unauthorized access.
boundary_definitions.name: Storage encryption

boundary_definitions.description: Security events and forensic evidence are generated and preserved.
known_exclusions: preventive controls merely named in an audit event
boundary_definitions.name: Security audit

boundary_definitions.description: Password authentication resists guessing and weak-secret selection.
boundary_definitions.name: Password authentication strength

boundary_definitions.description: Use of external, consumer, or peer-provided online identities is explicitly accepted or rejected at a trust boundary.
boundary_definitions.name: External identity authentication

boundary_definitions.description: Authentication mechanisms that expose replayable or plaintext secrets are rejected.
known_exclusions: transport settings that carry no credentials
boundary_definitions.name: Weak and plaintext authentication

boundary_definitions.description: Activation of dormant privileged authority requires an independent approval boundary.
boundary_definitions.name: Privileged role activation

boundary_definitions.description: Authentication requires independent evidence beyond a single credential across the intended access scope.
known_exclusions: method registration, capability reporting, or terminology without access enforcement
boundary_definitions.name: Multifactor authentication enforcement

boundary_definitions.description: Authentication uses verifier-bound cryptographic proof that resists deceptive-origin capture, replay, and proxying.
known_exclusions: ordinary MFA whose factor can be phished, relayed, or replayed
boundary_definitions.name: Phishing-resistant authentication

boundary_definitions.description: Access policy requires a defined minimum authentication strength and refuses methods below it.
known_exclusions: method preference, registration, or inventory without enforcement
boundary_definitions.name: Authentication-strength enforcement

boundary_definitions.description: Continued access remains backed by sufficiently fresh authentication and protected continuation.
known_exclusions: fixed session cosmetics, sign-in logging alone, and risk-adaptive revalidation without a base session policy
boundary_definitions.name: Session assurance and authentication freshness

boundary_definitions.description: Authenticated state cannot be silently transferred or replayed outside its originating device, channel, or session context.
known_exclusions: transport encryption without token or session context binding
boundary_definitions.name: Authentication transfer and session binding
required_security_effects: authenticated state bound to originating context
technology_scope: token and session based authentication systems

boundary_definitions.description: Authentication policy admits device-dependent access only after validating trusted device identity and asserted device state.
known_exclusions: license entitlement, device enrollment, or compliance evaluation without authentication enforcement
boundary_definitions.name: Managed-device authentication trust
required_security_effects: device trust policy enforced at authentication

capabilities.definition: Establish and verify identities while resisting authentication misuse.
capabilities.name: Identity and authentication protection
capabilities.security_objective: Only authenticated and authorized identities gain access.

capabilities.definition: Protect reusable secrets and credential derivatives throughout their lifecycle.
capabilities.name: Credential protection
capabilities.security_objective: Credential material remains unavailable to unauthorized actors.

capabilities.definition: Mediate transitions into elevated execution contexts.
capabilities.name: Privileged execution control
capabilities.security_objective: Privileged actions require an enforced authorization boundary.

capabilities.definition: Restrict network paths crossing a protected system boundary.
capabilities.name: Network boundary protection
capabilities.security_objective: Only intended traffic reaches protected network services.

capabilities.definition: Protect administrative access through remote-management channels.
capabilities.name: Secure remote management
capabilities.security_objective: Remote administration is authenticated, authorized, and transport protected.

capabilities.definition: Control whether executable content may run.
capabilities.name: Application and code execution control
capabilities.security_objective: Only trusted and authorized code executes.

capabilities.definition: Prevent, contain, and respond to malicious software behavior.
capabilities.name: Malware prevention and response
capabilities.security_objective: Malicious behavior is blocked or contained before material impact.

capabilities.definition: Provide confidentiality, integrity, and peer authenticity through cryptographic mechanisms.
capabilities.name: Cryptographic and transport protection
capabilities.security_objective: Information is protected in transit and at cryptographic trust boundaries.

capabilities.definition: Preserve visibility and evidence for detecting and investigating security events.
capabilities.name: Security monitoring and investigation
capabilities.security_objective: Security-relevant activity is observable and attributable.

capabilities.definition: Protect data against unauthorized disclosure, alteration, and loss.
capabilities.name: Data protection
capabilities.security_objective: Stored and processed data retains confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
